hints.title: Binary Suffix Parity Elimination
hints.text: Even numbers allow dividing by 2, clearing the lowest zero bit. For odd numbers, adding 1 or subtracting 1 changes the binary suffix structure.

hints.title: Two-Bit Lookahead Greedy Rule
hints.text: When n is odd, consider n modulo 4. If n % 4 == 3 and n is not 3, adding 1 produces two trailing zeros, reducing steps faster than subtracting 1.

hints.title: Iterative 64-Bit Simulation
hints.text: While n exceeds 1: if n is even, divide by 2. If n is 3 or n % 4 == 1, decrement n; otherwise increment n. Count each operation.

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unbounded recursive branching explores 2^(log N) paths without pruning, leading to slow exponential execution.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: The two-bit lookahead greedy rule resolves each step deterministically in O(1) time with zero extra allocations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that 3 is a special base case where decrementing is strictly better than incrementing.
